lines.text: Dutch people can be very direct: they often honestly say what they really think, but they usually try to do so in a friendly way.
Example: a colleague simply says 'Sorry, I'm not coming' to an invitation, or gives criticism [kritiek] on your work and says how it could be better.
Not everyone in the Netherlands acts and thinks the same.

There are differences between: old and young people; people from different cultures [culturen]; people from a city and from a village; people from different regions [regio's] — for example the north or the south; people with different political ideas; people with a religion [geloof] — Muslims, Christians, Jews — or without religion; people with a theoretical [theoretische] or a practical education [praktische opleiding].

If you don't know what the customs [gewoontes] are (bring a gift? take off your shoes? arrive exactly on time? how long to stay?), you can simply ask [vragen], for example: 'Shall I come alone or bring my partner?' You can also watch what others do, or look something up on the internet.
